thing: a boatman's house near the city landing, with a room inside and a locked back room
why: Not met. The house nearest the city landing, about 50 metres from where the raft-master stands, now shows "Ixtul-Bei's House" on its door, and inside its one room stands a locked chest (Novice) the household owns, which the story can use in place of a back room. Nothing marks it as a boatman's: Ixtul-Bei is the tally-keeper.
fit: That house (the tally-keeper Ixtul-Bei's household lives there today) could be the spies' house: the story can meet them in its one room. The boatmen's lodge, a moored ship about 76 metres from the landing whose door shows "Ship", is the other building a player would tie to boatmen.
narrow: Partly. A name on the house (the name its door shows) and the household's people placed inside are narrow changes. A locked back room is not: the house has one room, so the story should keep its secret behind a locked chest or a locked door the room already has.
sight_said: none (second reading 2026-11-13, after the rooms were named and the spring and chest placed): a house by name, far from the landing as the reader judged it, not tied to a boatman

thing: the city tree's spring shut behind a low wicker door that locks, with a dipper on its lip and a guard's post beside it
why: Met as a sealed spring. A lidded clay urn the game names "Sealed Spring", locked at Novice and owned by the town, stands at the foot of the sacred tree, 5 metres east of its trunk. No wicker door, dipper or guard post is there: the story names what is placed. The nearest guard stand is about 98 metres away.
fit: The sacred tree itself, where most of the townsfolk stand by day, among them the water-carrier who says the spring is not used. The story could put the shut water at the tree's foot as a sealed basin or a locked water jar, guarded by one of the levy.
narrow: Yes, as placed things: a basin or small pool piece and a wicker gate that locks at the tree's foot, and one guard's day spot moved beside it. No redraft. If no piece we hold reads as a spring, the story should name what is placed instead (a sealed basin).
sight_said: second reading 2026-11-13, after the rooms were named and the spring and chest placed: the Sealed Spring, locked, beside the Hist tree; no wicker door, dipper or guard seen

thing: the tree-minders' hall as a building that can be entered, with a place inside where Okeeh-Ja stands
why: Met. The cave at the north-west edge, by the waterfalls, shows "Tree-Minders' Hall" on its door and inside; the healer Taleeka-Ma heals and sells spell tomes there beside the arcane enchanter, and two guards stand at its mouth. The faction's leader is not yet placed inside.
fit: The cave itself: it can be entered, the healer already works there by the enchanter the town promises for its hall, and the faction's leader could stand inside. The story can call it the tree-minders' cave, or keep 'hall' once the name is changed. It is about 520 metres from the sacred tree.
narrow: Yes: renaming the room (the name its door shows) to "Tree-Minders' Hall" is a narrow change, and it also takes away the test name a player would see today; the leader is one person placed inside.
sight_said: second reading 2026-11-13, after the rooms were named and the spring and chest placed: Tree-Minders' Hall, a healers' hall; Taleeka-Ma inside read as its leader

thing: Xilsa-Jee and Hixee-Ra where they already stand by day, in the crowd at the sacred tree in the middle of the town
why: Met. Xilsa-Jee, the young root-tender, and the elder Hixee-Ra both stand by day in the crowd round the sacred tree, where a player can speak to them.

thing: the Xeech-Leel's council house (a building Helstrom does not have): a hall open by day, the treasurer's room upstairs, a front door, a back door to the river landing (an Expert lock), a gallery door reached up the stilts, a strongroom behind an iron door (a Master lock) with the gold, the seal ring and the silver, six wardens at night, and the cook (to be added to Helstrom: its source has only a one-room house and a ship, so the building is made from Dragonthorn Manor of King of the Murkmire's Lilmoth with its barracks for the wardens, and the strongroom is added as one locked iron door and a room of Imperial pieces)
why: Met for the place's part. A Murkmire house south-east of the sacred tree, reached over the boardwalk off its porch, shows "The Council House of the Xeech-Leel" on its front door and opens on a copy of Dragonthorn Manor (the hall with writing desks and silver, the upper room that serves as the treasurer's, partition doors), open by day. A back door in its back wall, locked at Expert, opens towards the wardens' quarters; in the hall's back wall an Imperial iron door locked at Master leads to the Council Strongroom (a copy of Journey to Baan Malur's stone cellar). Six wardens keep the night watch round the house and sleep by day in the Council Wardens' Quarters (a copy of Dragonthorn Manor Barracks); the cook Gathe-Ru works in the hall. The gallery door up the stilts is the story's FreeClimb way in (thieves.md:333): the stilts and the upper floor's windows are there to climb, and no stair is added for it. The gold, seal ring and silver are the quest's own things.
narrow: Nothing more to change for the place.
sight_said: A big council hall plus a guard post; its door reads Council House of the Xeech-Leel, it has a Council Strongroom door, and wardens stand outside.

thing: a quiet house south of the city tree by the city landing, its door showing "Nesh-Deeka's House" (the source city's one-room Argonian house 8, with its tables, benches, beds, enchanter and locked chest), where the handler, Nesh-Deeka, stands by the table and Never-Writes-Twice at the back
why: Met. The one-room Argonian house nearest the city landing now shows "Nesh-Deeka's House" on its door; its household is hers alone, with Never-Writes-Twice as its lodger (the quest keeps her disabled until quest 10). The room holds three tables, two chairs and three benches, six beds, four dressers, two workbenches, an arcane enchanter, an iron door and a locked chest the household owns; the other residents left the city's people. Nesh-Deeka's own spot by the table is the quest's placement.
sight_said: A small residential hut called Nesh-Deeka's House, with beds, an enchanter and a locked chest; the door is named for her.

thing: the Unbound go-between, Keel-Raa, lodging at the Boatmen's Lodge, the city's inn (the source's ship interior), among the crates at the far end of the hold, with his two hired men beside him, and his pack (a knapsack he owns, Skyrim's container) on the crates behind them with a jar of stolen sap in it
why: Met for the place's part. The moored ship's hold shows "Boatmen's Lodge" on its door and is the city's inn, kept by Sleeps-Last; its far end, 6 to 7 metres from the door, holds a long crate, a shelf and stacked crates. Keel-Raa, his two hired men and his pack with the jar of sap are the quest's own placements among those crates.
fit: The go-between and his men can stand at the far end of the hold among the crates, or by the end table and the bed.
narrow: Yes, if a table is wanted: one table placed by hand at the far end of the hold (draft.add) is a narrow change.
sight_said: The Boatmen's Lodge, a ship-shaped inn by the docks; rent a bed and buy food and drink from Sleeps-Last (the go-between and his men are the quest's own placements).

thing: the tree-minders' hall (an added interior built from King of the Murkmire's Hist-root pieces) with its arcane enchanter, Okan-Zeel, the order's enchanter and an urn niche
why: Met for the place's part. The mossy cave mouth in its mud rocks west of the city tree's plaza shows "Tree-Minders' Hall" on its door; inside the door stand the arcane enchanter and, beside it, a chest the game names "Urn Case", locked at Expert and owned by the town, which serves as the urn's niche. The hall is the source city's own cave, not built from King of the Murkmire's Hist-root pieces as the story words it; a player meets a hall of the order either way. Okan-Zeel, the two grave-singers and the urn itself are the quests' own placements and thing.
fit: The hall's entrance, beside the enchanter, where the healer Taleeka-Ma already works.
narrow: Yes: one container placed by hand and its lock; nothing else changed.
sight_said: The Tree-Minders' Hall: its door is named for it and it holds an Arcane Enchanter and a locked Urn Case; spells and training from Taleeka-Ma.

thing: the treasurer in the market by day; a raft-master at the city landing (the market square and the root landing are additions that the place's record lists)
why: Met for the place's part. The raft-master Poles-Upriver works at the city landing, and the market (the Market Cave with its stalls, and the traders round the sacred tree) is there by day. The treasurer is the quest's own placement, walking the market by day.
fit: The landing and the market as they stand.
sight_said: A river dock with a boatwoman, Poles-Upriver, who offers passage by boat to other towns; the town's traders by the Hist tree are the nearest market.

sight_said: The town centre at the Hist tree; the map marks Helstrom and the Rootworm Landing here (the root-tender works at the landing by reference to its mouth, which the sheet does not list).

Seen from the landing and from the log walk.
